Here we report the first detection of a hot molecular core in the extreme outer Galaxy, which is an excellent laboratory to study star formation and interstellar medium in a Galactic low-metallicity environment.

Our ALMA observations have detected a variety of carbon-, oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulfur-, and silicon-bearing species, including complex organic molecules (COMs) containing up to nine atoms, towards a warm ($>$100 K) and compact ($<$ 0.03 pc) region
Fractional abundances of CH$_3$OH and other COMs relative to H$_2$ generally scale with the metallicity of WB89-789, which is a factor of four lower than the solar value.
A comparison of fractional abundances of COMs relative to the CH$_3$OH column density between the outer Galactic hot core and a Galactic intermediate-mass hot core show a remarkable similarity.

all_quotes.quote: The H$_2$CO column density derived in this work may be a lower limit because the line is often optically thick, thus we do not discuss the abundance ratio relative to H$_2$CO.

all_quotes.loc: Another embedded protostar traced by high-velocity SiO gas
all_quotes.quote: We note that the detailed structure of high-velocity SiO gas is not spatially resolved, and CO lines, which often trace high-velocity outflows, are not covered in the present data.
